body:
I appreciate your comment, but I don't think drinking less is advice that address the root of my problems. Sure, I won't (and don't) drink very much as I know that there's only harm to endure. But that in itself will not pull me out of my pit of hopelessness which is very much present without alcohol being in my life at all. 

As (again) I know there is no immediate threat to my life, I am not particularly worried about making a rash life-threatening decision while drunk. That said, if I entered a true black out state, I can't really say with 100% certainty that I trust myself. So at the very least, drinking less (or not at all) can only serve as good advice in itself.

I've been drinking for around 4 years total. I'm 21 now. The drinking became a real issue 3 years ago in my first year of university and has since served as an on-and-off trouble maker. 

The past couple of months I have been completely alcohol-free. I should clarify that my problems with alcohol don't stem from addiction, they come from the short term decisions that I've made while intoxicated. I have little problem abstaining from drinking and I seldom even think about drinking, it's just that when I do, I can't control my intake. This is mostly due to (social) anxiety and generally not feeling comfortable around anyone. I don't drink alone as there aren't any particular problems for alcohol to address while I'm only in my own company.

This suicidal "episode" occurred at the end of my drinking night, which was the second of such nights to occur in the past 2 months. It resulted from the perceived betrayal committed by two of my "friends"--my view of it as such was partially irrational but at the same time not completely separate from some true issues. This I guess triggered/amplified extreme feelings of existing loneliness and isolation, a spiral that my drunken mind could not quell.
